name: ai-citations

frames.best_why: The whole answer is shown with an open source preview and its backing sentence highlighted.

tagline: Hover a tiny source chip and its sentence lights up as a card glides in.
summary: An AI answer paragraph with small source chips after cited claims. Hovering or focusing a chip highlights that sentence in blue and floats a preview of the source's site, title and snippet.
appearance: A left-aligned block of light grey text on black, with faint underlined claims and pale rounded chips carrying a lettered badge and a site name. Overlapping circular badges sit below beside 4 sources and a chevron; a rounded card with source rows floats above the text.
behaviour: Pointing at or focusing a chip tints the claim it supports blue and glides a preview card above or below it. Moving between chips slides the same card across, while leaving, pressing Escape or tapping elsewhere closes it; the sources row expands into a numbered link list.
demo_content: Advice on fast UI motion citing emilkowal.ski, web.dev and MDN; the footer reads 4 sources.
search_phrases: inline citation chips in a reply
highlight sentence when source is hovered
cite sources inline in answer text
click a source to see its snippet
use_when: An AI answer draws on the web and each claim needs a visible, checkable source.
avoid_when: Cramped reading areas: the floating preview covers the paragraph it is meant to explain.
customise: The answer parts and the sources are arrays of props; citation order and badge tints are derived, while card width and delays are constants in the source.
weight_why: A paragraph, a handful of chips and one animated popover; nothing runs while it is closed.

a11y.note: Chips are labelled buttons, focus opens the preview and Escape closes it; reduced motion is honoured.

issues: The floating preview card hides the words of the paragraph behind it.
polish_why: Citations read naturally in the prose and the preview glides well; the card covers nearby text.
